items.gist: Śaktipāta is not attained merely by boasting qualities; even one initiated may not gain liberation. Mantras bind the initiate in the house of worldly existence, while the guru's grace-śakti liberates.
The rite purifies and arranges nyāsa, then performs homa with sruksruvā and clarified offerings, directing prāṇa and mantra into the fire up to the dvādaśānta.
The text maps sky, māyā, bindu, nāda, ātman, śakti, and Śiva through vyāpya-vyāpaka relations, extending down to pṛthvī and the tattva series.
After establishing the fire, caru and vīra-dravyas are offered; the rite culminates in samāpāta, uniting bhoktṛ and bhogya through mantra and offering.
The guru initiates disciples through pañcagavya, caru, sprinkling, and controlled vision, leading them to perceive mantra-presence and become mantra-saturated.
The guru places the mantra-cakra on the disciple's hand and head, conferring samayī status and loosening tattva-pāśa through Śiva's hand.
The sādhaka becomes an ācārya through abhiṣeka and mastery of mantras, tantras, and paths; samayī status grants authority across the three grades.
After śivahasta purification, the disciple is settled in meditation, then placed in a mantra-empowered bed; sleep and dream become luminous, culminating in the dvādaśānta vision.
